quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: When braking and weight moves to the front of your bike, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry. Weight transfer does not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, slowly add more pressure to the front brake lever as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the motorcycle.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without getting in the driver's way. Hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you away from other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and avoid hazards. It also keeps an escape route open in case of danger. It should not block your escape route.

questions.question: When making normal stops, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for regular stops.

questions.question: Before entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cause of motorcycle wobble?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Improper loading
Unsuitable accessories
Uneven road

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: To work properly, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Prevent all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Block your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air through to prevent fogging, and fit eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: The best way to brake in a straight line is to use both brakes together. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which is NOT something you should tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and still so you can focus on riding. They should only get on after the engine starts, sit far forward, and hold on firmly to you.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever quickly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Push harder and harder on the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: To stop safely, squeeze the brakes smoothly and firmly. As you brake, more weight moves forward, giving you more grip at the front wheel. You can then use more front brake and less rear brake. Keep your knees against the tank and your eyes up to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Go faster.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks made by cars. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Only use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Do one action first, then do the other.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve left, press the left handgrip lightly, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor that affects blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The person's body weight
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three things affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. How often you drink does not affect your BAC. Never ride under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When packing items on a motorcycle, where should the heavier items go?

options.text: Toward the front.
Toward the rear.
Behind the rear axle.
In front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the front.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not used to them, why should you practice?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
Convex mirrors make things look farther away than they really are.
Convex mirrors make things look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to check mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Convex mirrors make things look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you. But they make objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors before riding.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve, what happens?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be careful. Your tires are already using grip to turn, so less grip is left for braking.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. But in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does the lead rider mean by raising their left arm with one finger extended?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Form a single-file line.
The group will exit soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Form a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm with one finger extended, it means all riders should form a single-file line.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly and gradually increase front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Accelerate before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching dangerous areas like intersections, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: How can you reduce the time needed to react to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces reaction time when a hazard appears.

questions.question: When the road is wet, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
All portions equally.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. When the road is wet, this oily strip becomes slippery. You can ride safely on either side of this center strip and still stay in the lane.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do when looking through turns?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes.
questions.explanation: Always look where you want to go through turns. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: If a driver is following too closely, flash your brake light before you slow down. This warns them that you are stopping for a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Give you an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen better. It should keep you out of blind spots, avoid wind blasts, and provide an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.
